blocks.text: Can a fully synthetic multi-cohort benchmark exercise evidence-linked poster generation without redistributing a real paper?
Fixed seed -> 1,240 profiles and 480 anonymous features -> nested elastic-net selection -> 12-feature AURORA-12 score -> four-cohort stress testing.
Four deterministic synthetic cohorts contained 620 discovery, 310 internal-validation, 186 external-A and 124 external-B profiles; total n=1,240.
AURORA-12 C-indices were 0.78, 0.76, 0.75 and 0.74, compared with 0.68, 0.67, 0.66 and 0.65 for the synthetic baseline.
External calibration slopes were 0.97 and 0.95, with absolute errors of 0.031 and 0.038; aggregate coefficient-sign stability was 92% across 500 resamples.
The most severe pre-specified synthetic shift reduced C-index by 0.04 from the matched reference simulation.
Every value is authored and synthetic; no biological transportability, prognosis, treatment effect or clinical utility may be inferred.
AURORA-12 is a controlled, rights-safe evaluation fixture for evidence-linked scientific communication and poster rendering.
